p.src: Now, just as Xifeng was getting up, still puzzled by what had happened, the little maid’s words gave her another fright, and she hurriedly asked, “What official business?” “I don’t know either,” replied the little maid. “A moment ago a page from the inner gate came in and reported that there was urgent official business for Master Zheng, so Her Ladyship sent me to ask Second Master Lian to come.” When Xifeng heard that it was business concerning the Ministry of Works, she felt somewhat relieved and said, “Go back and tell Her Ladyship that Second Master Lian went out of the city on business last night and has not returned. “Send someone to fetch Cousin Zhen first.” The maid acknowledged the order and left.

p.src: Before long Jia Zhen arrived, met the men from the ministry, and learned the details. He then went in to see Lady Wang and reported, “The ministry has sent word that yesterday the Director-General of the Yellow River memorialized the throne that an embankment had burst in the Henan region, inundating several prefectures and counties. “State funds must also be disbursed to repair the city fortifications. “The officials of the Ministry of Works will have many arrangements to make, and so the ministry sent someone expressly to inform Master Zheng.” Having said this, he withdrew, and when Jia Zheng returned home, the matter was reported to him. From then until winter, Jia Zheng had official business every day and was often at his ministry office. The supervision of Baoyu’s studies consequently grew more relaxed; but for fear that Jia Zheng might discover this, Baoyu dared not neglect his regular attendance in the schoolroom, and did not even dare visit Daiyu very often.

p.src: By then it was already the middle of the tenth month. Baoyu rose and prepared to go to the schoolroom. The weather had suddenly turned cold that day, and Xiren had already prepared a bundle of clothes. She said to Baoyu, “It is very cold today. Morning and evening, it is better to dress too warmly than not warmly enough.” As she spoke, she took out the clothes and selected one garment for Baoyu to wear. She wrapped up another garment, had a little maid take it out to Beiming, and instructed him, “The weather is cold. Keep this ready in case Second Master wishes to change.” Beiming acknowledged her instructions, took the felt bundle in his arms, and followed Baoyu away. Baoyu reached the schoolroom and completed his assigned work. Suddenly he heard the wind rattling loudly against the paper windows. “It is turning cold again,” said Dairu. He pushed open the wind door and looked out. Layer upon layer of black clouds in the northwest were gradually sweeping toward the southeast. Beiming came in and said to Baoyu, “Second Master, it has grown colder. You had better put on another layer.” Baoyu nodded. Beiming brought in a garment. The instant Baoyu saw it, he fell into a trance. All the younger pupils stared wide-eyed: it was the peacock-gold cloak that Qingwen had mended. “Why did you bring this one?” cried Baoyu. “Who gave it to you?” “The young ladies inside wrapped it up and sent it out,” replied Beiming. “I am not very cold,” said Baoyu. “I will not wear it yet. Wrap it up again.” Dairu assumed that Baoyu was reluctant to spoil so fine a garment, and inwardly approved of his newfound thrift. “Please put it on, Second Master,” said Beiming. “If you catch cold, your servant will be blamed again. “Wear it, if only out of kindness to your servant.” Baoyu had no choice but to put it on, and sat staring blankly at his book. Dairu merely thought he was reading and paid him little attention. When lessons ended that evening, Baoyu pleaded illness to Dairu and asked for a day’s leave. Dairu was already advanced in years and taught the few children mainly to relieve his boredom. Since he himself was frequently plagued by one ailment or another, he was quite pleased to have one pupil fewer to worry about for a day. Besides, he knew perfectly well that Jia Zheng was busy and that Grandmother Jia doted on Baoyu, so he nodded his assent.

p.src: Baoyu went straight home and, upon seeing Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, gave them the same explanation. Naturally neither doubted him. After sitting with them briefly, he returned to the Garden. When he saw Xiren and the others, he neither talked nor laughed as he usually did, but lay down fully dressed on the kang. “Dinner is ready,” said Xiren. “Would you like to eat now, or wait a while?” “I will not eat,” said Baoyu. “I do not feel well. “You go and eat.” “Even so, you ought to take off that cloak,” said Xiren. “A thing like that cannot bear being crushed and rubbed.” “There is no need to change it,” said Baoyu. “It is not only that the material is delicate,” said Xiren. “Look at the needlework on it—you should not treat that so carelessly either.” Her words struck Baoyu directly in the heart. He sighed and said, “In that case, put it away and wrap it up carefully for me. I will never wear it again.” As he spoke, he stood and took it off. By the time Xiren came over to take it, Baoyu had already begun folding it himself. “How is it that Second Master has become so diligent and careful today?” asked Xiren. Baoyu made no reply. When he had finished folding it, he asked, “Where is the cloth it was wrapped in?” Sheyue hastily handed it to him and let him wrap the cloak himself; then she turned and exchanged a wink and a smile with Xiren. Baoyu paid them no attention and sat there listlessly. Suddenly the clock on its stand struck. He lowered his head to look at his watch and saw that its hands pointed to the second quarter after the beginning of the Hour of the Cock. Presently a little maid came and lit the lamps. “If you will not eat dinner, at least have a little congee,” said Xiren. “Do not simply starve yourself. Take care you do not bring on a fever from an empty stomach; then we shall have another burden on our hands.” Baoyu shook his head. “I am not very hungry. If I force myself to eat, I shall only feel worse.” “If that is so,” said Xiren, “you may as well retire early.” Xiren and Sheyue therefore prepared his bedding, and Baoyu lay down. He tossed and turned, unable to sleep; only as dawn approached did he finally doze off, but before the time it would take to eat a meal had passed, he was awake again.

p.src: By this time Xiren and Sheyue were both awake as well. Xiren said, “Last night I heard you tossing and turning until the fifth watch, but I did not dare ask what was wrong. Later I fell asleep myself, so I do not know whether you ever managed to sleep.” Baoyu replied, “I slept for a little while, but somehow I woke again.” Xiren asked, “Are you feeling unwell anywhere?” “No,” said Baoyu. “I only feel terribly restless at heart.” Xiren asked, “Will you go to school today?” Baoyu replied, “I already took a day’s leave yesterday. Today I should like to spend the day wandering in the garden to clear my mind, only I am afraid of the cold. Have them prepare a room, set out a burner of incense, and lay out paper, ink, brushes, and inkstone. You may all attend to your own work; I want to sit quietly by myself for half the day. Do not let anyone come and disturb me.” Sheyue chimed in, “If Second Master means to apply himself in peace, who would dare disturb him?” Xiren said, “That would be very well, and it would keep you from catching cold. Sitting quietly by yourself will keep your thoughts from straying too.” Then she asked, “Since you have no appetite, what would you like to eat today? Tell me early, so I can send word to the kitchen.” Baoyu replied, “Anything will do. There is no need to make a great commotion over it. But put a few pieces of fruit in that room, so their fragrance will scent it.” Xiren asked, “Which room would be best? The others are none too clean. Only the room Qingwen used to occupy is still clean, since no one has lived there for some time, though it is rather cold and cheerless.” Baoyu said, “That does not matter. Just move the brazier in there.” Xiren assented. As they were speaking, a young maid came in carrying a tea tray with a bowl and a pair of ivory chopsticks. Handing it to Sheyue, she said, “This is what Miss Hua asked for just now. One of the women from the kitchen has brought it.” Sheyue took it and saw that it was a bowl of bird’s-nest soup. She asked Xiren, “Did you order this for yourself, sister?” Xiren smiled. “Second Master ate no supper last night and tossed about all night. I thought his stomach was sure to feel empty when he rose this morning, so I told the young maids to have the kitchen make this for him.” Xiren had a young maid set down a table, while Sheyue saw that Baoyu drank the soup and rinsed his mouth. Then Qiuwen came in and said, “The room is ready. Once the fierceness of the charcoal fire has died down a little, Second Master may go in.” Baoyu nodded, but his heart was so burdened with care that he had no wish to speak. Presently a young maid came to summon him, saying that the brushes and inkstone had all been set out. Baoyu said, “Very well.” Another young maid came to report, “Breakfast is ready. Where will Second Master take it?” Baoyu replied, “Just bring it here. There is no need for any further fuss.”

p.src: The young maid assented and went away. Before long breakfast was brought in. Baoyu smiled and said to Xiren and Sheyue, “I feel terribly oppressed. I am afraid I shall have no appetite if I eat alone. Why do you two not eat with me? If the meal seems more enjoyable, perhaps I shall eat a little more.” Sheyue laughed. “It is kind of Second Master to suggest it, but we would not dare.” Xiren said, “To tell the truth, there would be no harm in it. This is hardly the first time we have drunk wine together. It is all very well to cheer you up in this way now and then, but if we were to make a habit of it, what would become of proper decorum?” With that, the three of them sat down. Baoyu took the place of honor, while Xiren and Sheyue sat crosswise beside him. When they had finished eating, a young maid brought tea for rinsing their mouths, and the two women watched while everything was cleared away. Holding his tea, Baoyu sat silently, seemingly lost in thought. After sitting a little longer, he asked, “Is that room ready?” Sheyue replied, “We told you it was ready a while ago, and now you are asking again.”

p.src: Baoyu smiled and pretended to explain, “I was feeling troubled, so I found a quiet place where I could sit alone for a while. I feel better now, and I mean to take a walk outside.” With that, he came straight out and went to the Naiad’s House, where he stood in the courtyard and called, “Is Cousin Lin at home?” “Who is it?” Zijuan called back. She lifted the curtain to look and said with a smile, “Why, it’s Master Bao. Miss Lin is in her room. Please come inside and sit down, Master Bao.” Baoyu went in with Zijuan. Daiyu was in the inner room and called, “Zijuan, ask Master Bao to sit down in here.” At the entrance to the inner room, Baoyu saw a newly written couplet on small purple-inked, gold-flecked paper patterned with clouds and dragons: “At the green window the bright moon remains; in the blue annals, the ancients are gone.” Baoyu smiled when he read it, then entered and asked cheerfully, “What are you doing, Cousin?” Daiyu rose and came forward a couple of steps to greet him. “Please sit down,” she said with a smile. I am copying a scripture and have only two lines left. Let us talk after I finish them.” She then told Xueyan to pour the tea. “Don’t get up,” said Baoyu. “Just keep writing.” As he spoke, he noticed a narrow hanging scroll in the center. It depicted Chang’e with an attendant and another goddess, likewise attended, whose maid held something resembling a long garment bag. Wisps of cloud lightly encircled the two goddesses, but there was no other embellishment. The whole was executed in imitation of Li Longmian’s fine outline style, and the title “Contending with the Cold” was written above in clerical script. Baoyu asked, “Is this picture of yours, Contending with the Cold, newly hung?” “Yes, it is,” replied Daiyu. When they were tidying the room yesterday, I remembered it, took it out, and had them hang it up.” “What is its allusion?” asked Baoyu. Daiyu laughed. “It is something perfectly familiar, right before your eyes, and still you have to ask.” “I can’t recall it just now,” Baoyu said with a smile. “Do tell me.” Daiyu replied, “Have you not heard: ‘The Blue Maid and the Pale Beauty both withstand the cold, vying in loveliness amid moonlight and frost’?” “Of course!” said Baoyu. It really is novel and elegant, and this is just the right season to hang it.” As he spoke, he peered here and wandered there.

p.src: Baoyu asked, “Have you played the qin these last couple of days?” “I haven’t played for two days,” replied Daiyu. My hands already feel cold when I write, so how could I play the qin?” “It is just as well that you don’t,” said Baoyu. It seems to me that although the qin is a refined and lofty instrument, it is not a wholesome thing. No one has ever played wealth, honor, long life, or good health out of it; it produces only care, grief, resentment, and turmoil. Besides, playing requires you to keep the score in mind, which inevitably taxes your thoughts. In my opinion, since you are so frail, you had better spare yourself that worry.” Daiyu pursed her lips and smiled. Pointing at the wall, Baoyu asked, “Is that the qin? Why is it so short?” Daiyu smiled. “This qin is not short. When I began learning to play as a child, I could not reach across any of the others, so this one was specially made for me. Though its wood is neither the scorched tail nor the withered paulownia of legend, its Crane Mountain and Phoenix Tail are well matched, and the heights of its Dragon Pool and Wild-Goose Feet are properly proportioned. See how the markings in the wood resemble yak hairs? That is why its tone is still so pure and resonant.” Baoyu asked, “Have you written any poems these last few days?” “I haven’t written much since we formed the poetry club,” replied Daiyu. p.src: Zijuan answered and came out, only to find Xueyan standing there alone in a daze. Zijuan went up to her and asked, “Have you something troubling you now too?” Xueyan was so lost in thought that Zijuan startled her. She said, “Don't make a noise. I heard something today. Let me tell you, and you can judge how strange it is. But you mustn't say a word about it.” As she spoke, she jerked her chin toward the room. Then she walked ahead, nodding for Zijuan to follow her outside. Beneath the terrace by the door, she whispered, “Sister, haven't you heard? Baoyu is engaged!” Zijuan started at the news. “Where did such a story come from? Surely it can't be true.” “Why shouldn't it be true?” said Xueyan. “Everyone else probably knows. We are the only ones who haven't heard.” “Where did you hear it?” asked Zijuan. “I heard Shishu say it. The girl is from some prefect's family, and both her fortune and her qualities are said to be excellent.” As Zijuan listened, she suddenly heard Daiyu cough, as though she were getting up. Afraid Daiyu might come out and overhear them, Zijuan caught Xueyan by the arm and motioned for silence. She peered inside and, seeing no movement, whispered again, “What exactly did Shishu say?” Xueyan said, “Didn't they send me to thank the Third Young Lady the other day? She wasn't in her room, and only Shishu was there. As we sat together, the talk happened to turn to Master Bao's childish antics. She said that for all his good qualities, he only knew how to play and behaved nothing like a grown man; even though his marriage had already been arranged, he was still just as silly and muddle-headed. I asked whether it had really been settled. She said it had, and that a certain Mr. Wang had acted as matchmaker. This Mr. Wang is related to the family in the Eastern Mansion, so there was no need to make inquiries; the match was agreed as soon as it was proposed.” Zijuan tilted her head and thought for a moment. “That is a strange story!” Then she asked, “Why has no one in the household mentioned it?” Xueyan said, “Shishu said that was the Old Lady's wish. If the matter were spoken of, they were afraid Baoyu's thoughts would begin to wander, so no one mentions it. After telling me, Shishu repeatedly warned me never to let the secret out, for if it became known, everyone would say I had been gossiping.” She pointed inside. “That is why we don't mention it in front of her either. I am telling you today only because you asked; I wouldn't keep it from you.” Just then the parrot called out, mimicking the words, “Miss is back! Quick, pour the tea!” Zijuan and Xueyan both jumped. They turned but saw no one, so they scolded the parrot and went back into the room. They found Daiyu breathlessly settling into a chair. Trying to appear casual, Zijuan asked whether she wanted tea or water.

p.src: Daiyu asked, “Where did you two go? I called and called, but not one person came.” With that, she went over to the kang, let herself fall sideways upon it, and lay down again facing the wall, telling them to lower the bed curtains. Zijuan and Xueyan assented and went out. Both suspected that she might have overheard what they had just said, but neither dared mention it. Little did they know that Daiyu, already burdened with secret cares, had indeed listened to their conversation. Though she had not heard every detail clearly, she had understood most of it and felt as if she had been cast bodily into the vast sea. As she turned past and future over in her mind, it seemed that the omen in her recent dream had come true, and a thousand griefs and ten thousand bitter regrets crowded into her heart. Whichever way she considered it, she thought it better to die soon than to live to witness some unforeseen event and be left looking ridiculous. Then she reflected on the misery of having neither father nor mother. From now on, she would let her health waste away day by day; within six months or a year, surely she would attain final peace. Her mind made up, she neither drew the quilt over herself nor put on more clothes, but merely closed her eyes and pretended to sleep. Zijuan and Xueyan came in several times to attend her, but when she gave no sign of stirring, they did not dare call to her. She would not even eat her evening meal. After the lamps were lit, Zijuan lifted the bed curtain and saw that Daiyu appeared to be asleep, with the whole quilt kicked down beyond her feet. Afraid that she might catch cold, Zijuan gently pulled it up over her. Daiyu did not move, but as soon as Zijuan had gone out, she pushed it off again. Meanwhile Zijuan kept asking Xueyan, “Was what you said today really true or not?” “How could it not be true?” replied Xueyan. “How did Shishu know?” asked Zijuan. “She heard it from Xiaohong,” said Xueyan. Zijuan said, “I am afraid Miss may have overheard us earlier. Judging from the way she looked just now, something is certainly wrong. From today on, we had better say nothing more about it.” After this, the two of them also made ready for bed. When Zijuan went in to look, she saw that Daiyu had kicked off the quilt again, so she gently covered her with it once more. Nothing further need be said of that night.

p.src: Zijuan, standing beside her, did not dare offer any comfort, for fear that idle words might instead revive old grievances. Only after a long while did Daiyu casually wash and arrange her hair, but the traces of tears around her eyes never dried. After sitting alone for another while, she called to Zijuan, “Light the incense for me.” “Miss,” said Zijuan, “you have scarcely slept at all. Why light incense now? Surely you do not mean to copy sutras?” Daiyu nodded. Zijuan said, “You woke much too early today, Miss, and now you mean to copy sutras. I fear it will exhaust you.” “Never mind,” said Daiyu. “The sooner I finish, the better. Besides, it is not really for the sutra’s sake; I merely want to relieve my melancholy by writing. Hereafter, whenever you see my handwriting, you may count it as seeing my face.” As she spoke, tears streamed straight down her cheeks. Hearing this, Zijuan could no longer try to dissuade her; she could not even restrain her own tears from falling. Daiyu had in fact made up her mind deliberately to ruin her health from that time onward. She lost all interest in food and drink and consumed less with each passing day. When Baoyu returned from his lessons, he often found time to inquire after her. Yet though Daiyu had countless things she wished to say, she knew that they were now grown older and that she could no longer tease him with tender affection as she had in childhood; thus, all the feelings that filled her heart remained unspoken. Baoyu wished to tell her the truth and reassure her, but feared that Daiyu would take offense and that her illness would only worsen. Whenever they met, they could only exchange hollow words of consolation; truly, excessive intimacy had made them seem distant. Although Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others felt compassion for Daiyu, they did no more than summon physicians to treat her. They assumed it was merely her habitual illness and had no notion of the sickness in her heart. Though Zijuan and the other maids understood her meaning, they dared not speak of it. From then on, she ate less day by day. After half a month her stomach had grown so weak that one day she could not even swallow congee. By day, everything Daiyu heard seemed to concern Baoyu’s marriage; whenever she saw anyone from Happy Red Court, high or low, it too seemed to her part of the preparations for his wedding. When Aunt Xue came to see her without Baochai, Daiyu’s suspicions deepened. At last she refused all visitors and would take no medicine, desiring only a swift death. Even in her dreams, she often heard someone calling out, “Second Young Mistress Bao.” Her suspicions had conjured a serpent’s shadow where none existed. One day she stopped eating altogether and would not even drink congee. She lay faintly breathing, on the very verge of death. Whether Daiyu will live or die remains unknown; read the next chapter to learn what follows.
